per_option_rationale.rationale: Factoring the numerator but computing -(x-2) = 2-x at x=3, giving 2-3 = -1, an arithmetic slip in applying the factored form.
After cancelling (x-3), substituting x=3 into x (the original variable) rather than into (x-2), yielding 3 instead of 1.
Observing that x^2-5x+6 = 0 when x=3 and (x-3)=0 when x=3, then reporting 0/0 = 0 without factoring and cancelling.

explanation: Factoring the numerator as (x-2)(x-3) and cancelling the common factor (x-3) leaves lim(x->3)(x-2) = 1; the setup decision is recognising the trinomial factoring.

explanation_sections.punchline: When a trinomial numerator vanishes at the limit point, the limit point is always a root: factor it out to resolve the 0/0 form.
explanation_sections.approach: State the property then contrast the confusable one. Substitution gives 0/0, an indeterminate form. Setup decision: factor the trinomial. x^2-5x+6 has roots where sum=5 and product=6, so roots 2 and 3: (x-2)(x-3). Cancel (x-3): remaining factor is (x-2). Substitute x=3: 3-2=1. Contrast the trap: computing 2-x (wrong sign) gives -1, and reading x alone after cancellation gives 3.
explanation_sections.lesson: For lim(x->a) P(x)/(x-a) where P(a)=0: factor P as (x-a)*Q(x) and the limit equals Q(a).
explanation_sections.timing: About 75 seconds. Identify 0/0 (10 sec), factor trinomial (30 sec), cancel and substitute (20 sec). Main trap: sign flip when reading the remaining factor.
